doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Dallas memories and the Denver years
title: Ellis Marsalis and multi-instrumentalists in New Orleans
summary: Walton recalls Ellis Marsalis on bass, the New Orleans habit of playing several instruments, and a high-school gig with Harold Battiste; he met James Black and Nat Perrilliat's circle only later or not at all.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Um, just to go back to New Orleans, you mentioned Ellis; did you, you came into Dillard together, did you develop a relationship?
Was he playing saxophone or piano?

He was playing … uh, bass. I mean, uh, in fact, uh, which brings to mind, most of the musicians I've met when I went to New Orleans played more than one instrument. More than two. I said, "My God, [how they do that?]," you know, to myself. I didn't know you could do that, I mean, uh, I had studied bass in, in college but I mean, I would never try to play a gig. I couldn't last, probably, with the blisters. But uh, but these, these, these guys were playing more than just one, one instrument, you know like uh, enough to make a gig. I played a gig at some high school with Harold Battiste on the, whatever he was playin' that night, or one of the readers, and Ellis on bass and me on piano. That was my one outing in uh, New Orleans.
Did you meet James Bly? Did you ever hear about him down there?
Uh, I met him later. He wasn't around uh, during … 'cause I just stayed there one semester, and he might, I might have preceded him. I mean, yeah.
No, I, I, know the names but I got there and left before I met 'em. Yeah.
